questions.question: What are the tiny air sacs that make up the lungs called?
Where does gas exchange take place inside the human respiratory system?
options: Between air in alveoli and blood in capillaries
Between air in the trachea and blood in the heart
Between air in the bronchi and the pleural fluid
Between air in the diaphragm and muscle tissues

questions.question: Why do human lungs contain millions of alveoli instead of just a few large air sacs?
options: To protect the heart from physical injury
To increase the surface area of the lungs for gas exchange
To keep the chest cavity warm during exercise
To prevent dust particles from reaching the blood

questions.question: How does having alveoli walls that are only one cell thick benefit gas exchange?
options: It increases the pressure inside the lungs
It prevents carbon dioxide from leaving the blood
It creates a short diffusion distance for gas exchange
It allows blood cells to pass directly into the air sacs

questions.question: Why are alveoli surrounded by a dense network of blood capillaries?
options: To maintain a concentration gradient for gas exchange
To pump air directly into the bloodstream
To filter out pathogens before air reaches the heart
To hold the alveoli rigid during deep breathing

questions.question: Which gas is essential for aerobic cellular respiration to occur?
In which cellular structures does aerobic cellular respiration take place in animal, plant, and fungal cells?
Muscle cells do a lot of work and require large amounts of energy. What would you expect muscle cells to have more of compared to skin cells?
What products are made during anaerobic cellular respiration in microorganisms?
What is another term for anaerobic cellular respiration in microorganisms?
What defines anaerobic cellular respiration?
options: It takes place without using oxygen
It occurs only in plant roots
It creates glucose from carbon dioxide

questions.question: Which substance is produced during anaerobic cellular respiration in humans that can cause muscle cramps?
Where inside a cell does anaerobic cellular respiration take place?
options: Only in the cytoplasm of cells
In both the nucleus and mitochondria

questions.question: Compared to aerobic respiration, how does anaerobic cellular respiration differ in energy release?
options: It provides more energy, but more slowly
It provides less energy, but provides energy more quickly
It provides identical amounts of energy at the same speed
It provides more energy and works more quickly

questions.question: Which waste product is produced by cellular respiration and must be removed from the body?
During gas exchange in the human lungs, which direction do oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuses?
options: Oxygen diffuses from blood to lungs; carbon dioxide diffuses from lungs to blood
Oxygen diffuses from lungs into blood; carbon dioxide diffuses from blood into lungs
Both oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse from lungs into blood
Both oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse from blood into lungs

questions.question: Which reactant from food is used as fuel during cellular respiration to provide energy?
Which statement correctly describes when cellular respiration occurs?
options: Only in animals while they are sleeping
Only in plants during the night
In all living organisms all the time
Only in animals during intense exercise

questions.question: What is the vital capacity of the lungs?
options: The volume of blood surrounding the lungs
The maximum volume of air that can be exhaled after inhaling fully
The speed at which air moves through the trachea
The minimum volume of air left in the lungs after exhaling

questions.question: What does it mean for a measurement to be accurate?
options: It is closer to the true value
It gives a different result each time
